tgm010949.scope: Various competitive athletic events (as running, jumping, and weight throwing) performed on a running track and on the adjacent field.

tgm010951.label: Tracklaying vehicles
tgm010951.scope: For vehicles which use the endless belt principle for traction.

tgm010953.label: Traction engines
tgm010953.scope: Steam powered vehicles used to power agricultural machinery, includes engines which were built as steam traction engines but subsequently converted to diesel or petrol.

tgm010957.label: Trade cards
tgm010957.scope: Advertising cards issued or enclosed with such products as bread, cigarettes, and agricultural machinery. Use COLLECTING CARDS for cards not intended to be advertisements.

tgm010958.label: Trade catalogs
tgm010958.scope: Catalogs issued by manufacturers, retailers, and wholesalers to sell their products. They usually have illustrations and textual descriptions of items for sale.

tgm010964.label: Trademarks
tgm010964.scope: Symbols or combinations of symbols, letters, and other characters legally reserved to identify products and makers.

tgm010979.label: Tragedies
tgm010979.scope: For images representing dramatic productions or scenes (theatrical, film, radio, or television) which focuses on the downfall of a great person and disastrous or sorrowful conclusions.

tgm010980.label: Trailers
tgm010980.scope: Use for non-motorized wheeled vehicles that include a chassis and are primarily intended to be towed by other vehicles.

tgm010991.label: Traitors
tgm010991.scope: Search also under the subdivision --COLLABORATION used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm010997.label: Transfer lithographs
tgm010997.scope: A lithographic print produced when an image is drawn or printed on transfer paper and then transferred to the lithographic stone or plate for printing. The process of transfer lithography was used commercially from about 1850.

tgm010998.label: Transfer sheets
tgm010998.scope: Paper or other flexible sheets containing images intended for transfer to another surface by application of pressure, heat, or moisture. Examples include iron-on patterns and pictures on graphite paper.

tgm011002.label: Transformer rooms
tgm011002.scope: Rooms containing electric transformers and their auxilliary equipment.

tgm011010.label: Transmitted images
tgm011010.scope: Images converted to electronic signals for the purpose of sending them to a remote device for printing by an electrical, thermal, or other non-photographic process.

tgm011013.label: Transparencies
tgm011013.scope: Sheets of transparent material, such as glass, thin paper, or plastic, bearing a photographic, printed, or hand-drawn image and designed to be viewed by light shining through them; often intended for use with a projection device.

tgm011015.label: Transportation
tgm011015.scope: Search also under the subdivision --TRANSPORTATION used with names of indigenous peoples (Appendix A) and with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011017.label: Transportation industry
tgm011017.scope: Manufacture and trade of vehicles. Includes activities and structures.

tgm011019.label: Transporter bridges
tgm011019.scope: Bridges designed to span navigable waterways between low shores and made of a high framework from which is suspended a car for carrying traffic back and forth.

tgm011020.label: Transgender people
tgm011020.scope: Any individual who does not identify as the gender which they were assigned at birth.

tgm011031.label: Travel
tgm011031.scope: For the subject of travel in general. Search also under the subdivision --TRAVEL used with names of persons (Appendix B).

tgm011032.label: Travel posters
tgm011032.scope: Posters that promote general tourism or advertise travel opportunities. The means of transportation, such as railroads or ocean liners, are often depicted.

tgm011033.label: Travel sketches
tgm011033.scope: Sketches made of places, buildings, objects, people, or events seen during a journey; often made to record a particular feature for future reference.

tgm011041.label: Treasure troves
tgm011041.scope: Gold or silver in the form of money, plate, or bullion which is found hidden and whose ownership is not known.

tgm011043.label: Treaties
tgm011043.scope: Search also under the subdivision --TREATIES used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011056.label: Trellises
tgm011056.scope: Frames of latticework used as a screen or as support for climbing plants.

tgm011058.label: Trench warfare
tgm011058.scope: Search also under the subdivision --TRENCH WARFARE used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011059.label: Trestles
tgm011059.scope: For images that focus on the braced frameworks of timbers, piles, or steelwork, usually of considerable height, for carrying a road or railroad over a depression.

tgm011061.label: Trial proofs
tgm011061.scope: Prints made before the completion of the accepted impression.

tgm011075.label: Tricolor carbro prints
tgm011075.scope: Photographic prints made from color separation negatives printed as three bromide prints, each of which is then pressed against a sensitized carbon tissue of the appropriate color. The tissues are then superimposed to create the final color photograph. Chiefly used ca. 1900-1930s.

tgm011078.label: Trilithons
tgm011078.scope: Megalithic prehistoric structures of two upright stones and a lintel.

tgm011082.label: Triptychs
tgm011082.scope: Three separate images connected side by side (hinged or mounted) to form a single work. Often are paintings of devotional images used as alterpieces.

tgm011093.label: Trombones
tgm011093.scope: Includes the activity of playing trombones.

tgm011094.label: Trompongs
tgm011094.scope: A long percussion instrument comprised of a series of circular kettles used in Balinese gamelan music and dance.

tgm011096.label: Troop movements
tgm011096.scope: Shifting of troops from one location to another, as between battles. Search also under the subdivisions --AMPHIBIOUS OPERATIONS and --CAMPAIGNS & BATTLES used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011100.label: Trophies (Architectural ornaments)
tgm011100.scope: Architectural ornaments representing groups of military weapons.

tgm011102.label: Troubadours
tgm011102.scope: Medieval musical poets, often of knightly rank.

tgm011109.label: Truck industry
tgm011109.scope: Manufacture and trade of trucks. Includes activities and structures.

tgm011113.label: Trumpets
tgm011113.scope: Includes the activity of playing trumpets.

tgm011118.label: Truth
tgm011118.scope: A judgement, proposition, or idea that is true or accepted as true.

tgm011165.label: Tympana
tgm011165.scope: Recessed, usually triangular faces of pediments within the frame made by the upper and lower cornices; spaces within arches and above lintels or subordinate arches.

tgm011176.label: Typhoons
tgm011176.scope: Includes the event and any resulting damage.

tgm011184.label: Ukuleles
tgm011184.scope: Includes the activity of playing ukuleles.

tgm011186.label: Ukiyo-e
tgm011186.scope: An art genre from the Edo period (1600-1868) in Japan, mostly but not always in the medium of woodblock prints. The term Ukiyo-e means pictures of the floating or sorrowful world. Formats include single and multiple sheet works as well as book illustrations.

tgm011192.label: Unbuilt projects
tgm011192.scope: Illustrations or designs depicting architectural projects that were never built.

tgm011196.label: Underground literature
tgm011196.scope: For images that depict clandestine printing operations or the output of such operations, including illegal presses and anti-government literature or literature contrary to the regulations of an occupying force.

tgm011197.label: Underground movements
tgm011197.scope: Search also under the subdivision --UNDERGROUND MOVEMENTS used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011205.label: Underwater photographs
tgm011205.scope: Photographs made underwater with waterproof equipment or from a submarine or other vehicle.

tgm011206.label: Underwater photography
tgm011206.scope: For the subject of taking photographs underwater.

tgm011212.label: Unemployment
tgm011212.scope: For images that focus on social or economic impacts of unemployment. Use UNEMPLOYED for images of out-of-work or jobless people.

tgm011218.label: Uniforms
tgm011218.scope: Includes uniforms for sports and schools.

tgm011219.label: Union cases
tgm011219.scope: Thermoplastic cases introduced in the United States in 1852 for daguerreotypes and also made for ambrotypes and some tintypes through the 1860s. Almost 800 design motifs have been recorded. Often mistakenly referred to as gutta-percha cases.

tgm011223.label: Unitarian Universalist churches
tgm011223.scope: For images that focus on buildings, as well as the associated grounds.

tgm011247.label: Urban renewal
tgm011247.scope: Activity of clearing, rebuilding, restoring, or refurbishing urban areas.

tgm011250.label: Urns
tgm011250.scope: Vessels of various forms, usually with a foot or pedestal and used for holding liquids, for ornamental purposes, for preserving ashes of the dead after cremation and, anciently, for holding lots to be drawn.

tgm011281.label: Vandyke prints
tgm011281.scope: Photographic prints made by a formula introduced in the late 1800s. Used in the 1920s-1950s to reproduce architectural, engineering, and mechanical drawings. Mirror image white lines on a dark brown or sepia background were used to make blue or black line prints. Revived in mid-1960s as an alternative photographic process.

tgm011293.label: Vases
tgm011293.scope: For vessels, commonly decorative or for flowers.

tgm011296.label: Vaudeville shows
tgm011296.scope: Theatrical pieces, usually comic, consisting of dialogue or pantomime, intermingled with light songs and, sometimes, dances.

tgm011298.label: Vaults (Architecture)
tgm011298.scope: Arched structure, usually of masonry, and usually forming a ceiling or roof.

tgm011303.label: Vegetables
tgm011303.scope: For the subject of edible vegetables in general and images that focus on vegetables.

tgm011333.label: Veterans
tgm011333.scope: Search also under the subdivision --VETERANS used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011340.label: Veterinary medicine
tgm011340.scope: For the subject of veterinary medicine in general and the activities of veterinarians.

tgm011346.label: Vice presidents
tgm011346.scope: For the office of the vice president or for incumbents.

tgm011351.label: Victoria card photographs
tgm011351.scope: Card photographs; mounts measure approximately 5 x 3.5 in. (13 x 9 cm.). Introduced in the United States in 1870.

tgm011352.label: Victories
tgm011352.scope: Successes in any contests or struggles involving the defeat of an opponent or the overcoming of obstacles.

tgm011353.label: Victory celebrations
tgm011353.scope: Search also under the subdivision --PEACE used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011359.label: Videodiscs
tgm011359.scope: Analog optical disks primarily intended for the recording of photographs, prints, drawings, or other still or motion pictures as video signals. May include sound. The images are recorded by a laser and can be displayed on a video screen.

tgm011360.label: Viewbooks
tgm011360.scope: Published booklets and other volumes primarily consisting of views of particular places, events, and activities. May be photographs, photomechanical prints, or postcards; may be connected by accordion folds.

tgm011364.label: Views
tgm011364.scope: Depictions, in any media, usually of places and structures, made from a certain distance, and not necessarily intended to produce detailed information. Distinct from other information such as diagrams, working drawings, maps, and plans. A topographical image, showing a general aspect of a place.

tgm011371.label: Vigilance
tgm011371.scope: Keeping awake at times when sleep is customary, or periods of watching. Search under SURVEILLANCE for images related to law enforcement or criminal investigation.

tgm011374.label: Vigils
tgm011374.scope: Observances that are devotional, religious, political, or memorial in nature; also includes watching at bedside during times of illness.

tgm011375.label: Vignettes
tgm011375.scope: Engravings, photographs, and other pictures that shade off gradually into the surrounding image area. Often made to be combined with text or other illustration element.

tgm011379.label: Villages
tgm011379.scope: A unit of compact settlement, usually larger than a hamlet and smaller than a town, and distinguished from a surrounding rural area.

tgm011380.label: Villains
tgm011380.scope: Use for fictitious characters who do bad or evil, or for real people portrayed as such.

tgm011390.label: Violins
tgm011390.scope: Includes the activity of playing violins.

tgm011391.label: Violoncellos
tgm011391.scope: Includes the activity of playing violoncellos.

tgm011396.label: Visiting cards
tgm011396.scope: Small cards bearing a person's name and sometimes address; presented when making a formal social call. May have a portrait, scene, or decoration; may be accompanied by an envelope.

tgm011400.label: Visits of state
tgm011400.scope: Search also under the subdivision --TRAVEL used with names of persons (Appendix B).

tgm011405.label: Vitrolite (Trademark)
tgm011405.scope: Thick, opaque structural glass used especially as an ornamental finish on surfaces exposed to the weather.

tgm011407.label: Vocational education
tgm011407.scope: Includes on-the-job training and other activities and structures.

tgm011410.label: Volcanic eruptions
tgm011410.scope: Includes the event and any resulting damage.

tgm011416.label: Volvelles
tgm011416.scope: Diagrams with movable discs, circles, or pointers bearing graduated or figured information that are rotated for the purpose of determining scientific, astrological, or other measurements.

tgm011428.label: Voussoirs
tgm011428.scope: Stones forming part of an arch; wedge-shaped, they make the arch self-supporting.

tgm011432.label: Vues d'optique
tgm011432.scope: Prints intended for viewing through an optical system such as a zogroscope that enhances the effect of perspective. Because the viewing device included a mirror, the lettering and image are usually laterally reversed. Common in the late 1700s in Europe for peep shows.

tgm011434.label: V-mail
tgm011434.scope: For mail during World War II which was microfilmed and recopied on paper as a way of reducing shipping costs.

tgm011444.label: Wainscoting
tgm011444.scope: The lower part of interior walls when specially decorated or faced; also the decoration adorning this part of a wall.

tgm011460.label: Wallpapers
tgm011460.scope: Decorative paper intended to cover the walls of a room.

tgm011461.label: Walls
tgm011461.scope: Vertical architectural members used to define and divide spaces.

tgm011466.label: Wanted posters
tgm011466.scope: Broadsides or posters describing criminals sought by law enforcement agencies. Often include offers of rewards.

tgm011468.label: War
tgm011468.scope: For the subject of war in general and for wars that cannot be identified by name. Search primarily under names of specific wars and relevant topical subdivisions (Appendix C). The subdivision --WAR is used with names of ethnic, racial and regional groups, and with classes of persons (Appendix A) only when the war cannot be identified.

tgm011471.label: War blackouts
tgm011471.scope: For periods of enforced darkness as a precaution against or practice for air raids.

tgm011473.label: War bonnets
tgm011473.scope: Headdresses consisting of feathers, fur, and sometimes horse hair and/or horns, worn by North American Indians.

tgm011474.label: War casualties
tgm011474.scope: For images that focus on dead and wounded persons. Search under MEDICAL ASPECTS OF WAR for relief and medical care of casualties. Search also under the subdivision --CASUALTIES or --MEDICAL ASPECTS used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011477.label: War correspondents
tgm011477.scope: Search also under the subdivision --COMMUNICATIONS used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011480.label: War crimes
tgm011480.scope: Search also under the subdivision --ATROCITIES used with names of wars.

tgm011481.label: War damage
tgm011481.scope: For images made to show damage or views after the fighting. Search also under the subdivision --DESTRUCTION & PILLAGE used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011483.label: War destruction & pillage
tgm011483.scope: For the general subject of looting and destruction of property in the context of war as well as specific acts of plundering. Search also under the subdivision --DESTRUCTION & PILLAGE used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011485.label: War games
tgm011485.scope: Umpired training maneuvers imitative of war, in which opposed forces engage in attack and defense with actual personnel and equipment.

tgm011488.label: War posters
tgm011488.scope: Posters issued to support military or civilian war efforts, including propaganda. Search under PROTEST POSTERS for posters that protest war.

tgm011491.label: War profiteering
tgm011491.scope: Making an unreasonable profit by taking advantage of a public need in time of war.

tgm011492.label: War rallies
tgm011492.scope: For events intended to rally support for war or to spur labor production on behalf of war. Search also under the subdivisions --ECONOMIC & INDUSTRIAL ASPECTS, --EQUIPMENT & SUPPLIES, --RECRUITMENT & ENLISTMENT, and --SOCIAL ASPECTS used with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011493.label: War relief
tgm011493.scope: Official or private aid to civilians during wars in the form of money or necessities.

tgm011497.label: War work
tgm011497.scope: For civilian work as part of a war effort. For the effect of war on industrial and commerical activity search under the subdivision --ECONOMIC & INDUSTRIAL ASPECTS or by ethnic, racial, regional groups, and classes of persons subdivisions used with names of specific wars (Appendix C). The subdivision --WAR used with the names of ethnic, racial and regional groups, and with classes of persons (Appendix A) is used only when the war cannot be identified.

tgm011511.label: Wash drawings
tgm011511.scope: Drawings made from diluted ink or watercolor applied with a brush; usually monochromatic or two color, such as brown and gray.

tgm011531.label: Watch papers
tgm011531.scope: Circular papers used to ensure a tight fit between inner and outer cases of a pocket watch. Often contain watchmaker's or watch owner's name.

tgm011545.label: Water carriers
tgm011545.scope: Persons who carry or transport water for distribution.

tgm011553.label: Water gardens
tgm011553.scope: Gardens incorporating fountains and pools in which aquatic and other water-loving plants are grown.

tgm011570.label: Water supply
tgm011570.scope: For the subject of water resources both superficial and underground, primarily for domestic, manufacturing, or agricultural purposes.

tgm011572.label: Water towers
tgm011572.scope: Towers or standpipes serving as a reservoir to deliver water at a required head. Search under FIREFIGHTING EQUIPMENT for fire apparatus having a vertical pipe which can be extended to various heights, and supplied with water under high pressure.

tgm011584.label: Waterfronts
tgm011584.scope: For images that focus on land beside water, whether inhabited or uninhabited.

tgm011598.label: Waterwheels
tgm011598.scope: Any wheel made to rotate by action of water.

tgm011599.label: Waterworks
tgm011599.scope: The system of reservoirs, channels, mains, and pumping and purifying equipment by which a water supply is obtained and distributed (as to a city).

tgm011607.label: Waxed paper negatives
tgm011607.scope: Paper negatives made using Gustave Le Gray's waxed paper process, introduced in 1851. More popular in England and France than in the United States. Replaced the calotype process.

tgm011624.label: Weddings
tgm011624.scope: Search also under the subdivision --MARRIAGE used with names of persons (Appendix B).

tgm011631.label: Welding
tgm011631.scope: Uniting metallic parts by heating and allowing the metals to flow together or by hammering or compressing with or without previous heating.

tgm011638.label: Wellheads
tgm011638.scope: The structure built over the top of a well.

tgm011643.label: Westerns
tgm011643.scope: For images representing dramatic productions or scenes (theatrical, film, radio, or television) which have frontier or American western settings. Frequently features cowboys, Native Americans, or pioneers.

tgm011645.label: Westward movement
tgm011645.scope: For the Westward expansion of the United States.

tgm011646.label: Wet collodion negatives
tgm011646.scope: Dominant glass negative process from its introduction in the United States ca. 1855 until replaced by a dry plate process in the 1880s. Its use continued for photolithographic printing plates until World War II. Distinguishable in part by creamy rather than grayish black tones and by presence of flow lines from hand coating of the emulsion.

tgm011657.label: Wheeled chairs
tgm011657.scope: Chairs for passengers, mounted on two or three wheels, and drawn, pushed, or pedaled by another person.

tgm011668.label: Whistle-stop campaigning
tgm011668.scope: Brief personal appearances or speeches, especially by a political candidate usually on the rear platform of a train during the course of a tour.

tgm011672.label: White man's burden
tgm011672.scope: The supposed duty of white people to manage the affairs of non-white people. Originated (1899) by Rudyard Kipling.

tgm011682.label: Wickiups
tgm011682.scope: Shelters having a usually oval base and a rough frame covered with reed mats, grass, or brushwood. Used by the nomadic Native Americans of the arid regions of the western and southwestern United States.

tgm011689.label: Wigwams
tgm011689.scope: Shelters of Native Americans of the Great Lakes region and eastward, having typically an arched framework of poles overlaid with bark, rush mats, or hides.

tgm011690.label: Wild cats
tgm011690.scope: Search also under specific species of wild cat.

tgm011701.label: Wind instruments
tgm011701.scope: Includes the activity of playing wind instruments.

tgm011707.label: Window cards
tgm011707.scope: Large cards containing advertisements for display in store windows, often measuring 18 x 22 inches.

tgm011709.label: Window displays
tgm011709.scope: For images that focus on window dressings and displays. Search under SHOW WINDOWS for windows as a part of mercantile facilities rather than their displays.

tgm011711.label: Window seats
tgm011711.scope: Freestanding or built-in benches in the recess of a window.

tgm011726.label: Wine labels
tgm011726.scope: Slips of paper or other material affixed or meant to be attached to a wine bottle for identification, description, or decoration.

tgm011743.label: Wire photographs
tgm011743.scope: Photographs scanned and converted to electrical signals, transmitted over wires, and then re-formed into images. [AAT]

tgm011757.label: Witnesses
tgm011757.scope: A person present at an event who is able to testify from personal observation.

tgm011765.label: Women
tgm011765.scope: This heading may be further subdivided by the subdivisions used for classes of persons (Appendix A). Search also under other headings beginning with WOMEN or WOMEN'S. Search also under the subdivision --WOMEN used with names of ethnic, racial, and regional groups (Appendix A) and with names of wars (Appendix C).

tgm011772.label: Women's rights
tgm011772.scope: For the constitutional and legal status and treatment of women.

tgm011779.label: Wood carving
tgm011779.scope: Fashioning or ornamenting objects of wood by cutting with a sharp implement held in the hand.

tgm011783.label: Wood engravings
tgm011783.scope: Relief prints made from wood blocks incised on the end grain.

tgm011787.label: Woodburytypes
tgm011787.scope: Continuous tone photomechanical prints made by a carbon process introduced in the United States in 1870. Used through the 1890s, mainly for book illustrations. Difficult to distinguish from actual photographic prints, although slight surface relief may be visible.

tgm011790.label: Woodcuts
tgm011790.scope: Relief prints made from wood blocks incised on the plank side.

tgm011792.label: Woodcutting
tgm011792.scope: For the activity of cutting, splitting, chopping, or sawing trees and branches.

tgm011798.label: Wooding stations
tgm011798.scope: Places near a riverbank where cut logs are kept before being transported downriver.

tgm011803.label: Woodwork
tgm011803.scope: For work made of wood, especially indoor fittings (e.g., moldings or stairways).

tgm011804.label: Woodworking
tgm011804.scope: The act, process, or occupation of working with wood.

tgm011813.label: Work ethic
tgm011813.scope: A belief in work as a moral good.

tgm011821.label: Working class
tgm011821.scope: For the class of people who work for wages, excluding managers and professionals; generally at lower end of economic scale.

tgm011823.label: Working drawings
tgm011823.scope: Graphic delineations showing all necessary information to complete a structure, system, or site. In architecture, an umbrella term for sets of drawings including elevations, plans, and sections provided by the architect for use by the builder, electrician, plumber, or other contractor or fabricator.

tgm011842.label: Worm's-eye views
tgm011842.scope: Views with a viewpoint well below normal eye level. [AAT]

tgm011895.label: Yokes
tgm011895.scope: Bar or frame used to carry a load, usually suspended in two equal portions on opposite sides of the body, or used to join draft animals.

tgm011896.label: Young adults
tgm011896.scope: For persons in the general age range of eighteen to twenty-five years. Search also under the subdivision --WOMEN used with ethnic, racial, and regional groups and with classes of persons (Appendix A). Search also under the subdivision --CHILDHOOD AND YOUTH used with names of persons (Appendix B).

tgm011901.label: Youth
tgm011901.scope: The quality or state of being young. Search under CHILDREN or YOUNG ADULTS for young people. Search also under the subdivision --CHILDHOOD & YOUTH used with names of persons (Appendix B).

tgm011909.label: Yurts
tgm011909.scope: A circular tent of skins stretched over a collapsible lattice framework.

tgm011913.label: Zincographs
tgm011913.scope: Lithographs made from zinc plates rather than stones.

tgm011914.label: Zionism
tgm011914.scope: Theory, plan, or movement for setting up a Jewish national or religious community in Palestine.

tgm011917.label: Zithers
tgm011917.scope: Includes the activity of playing zithers.

tgm011922.label: Zoology
tgm011922.scope: For the subject of zoology in general and the activities of zoologists.

tgm011926.label: Zouaves
tgm011926.scope: For the French infantry unit that wore a brillant uniform or any military unit that adopted the dress of the Zouaves.

tgm012043.label: Sheikhs
tgm012043.scope: The chief of an Arab family or tribe; the headman or chief of an Arab village. May also be the head of a Muslim religious order or community.

tgm012046.label: Gossiping
tgm012046.scope: Talking about other people, sometimes negatively.

tgm012047.label: Beehive houses
tgm012047.scope: Houses with a circular plan and a conical dome.

tgm012054.label: Animal husbandry
tgm012054.scope: Care of domestic animals, especially farm animals.

tgm012057.label: Obscenity
tgm012057.scope: Expressions considered lewd or offensive by prevalent cultural norms.

tgm012079.label: Red-light districts
tgm012079.scope: An area denoted by an abundance of sex-related businesses.

tgm012084.label: Badlands
tgm012084.scope: An area of irregularly eroded land formations.

tgm012117.label: Putti
tgm012117.scope: Depictions of children, usually naked and rotund boys, often with wings.

tgm012133.label: Caryatids
tgm012133.scope: A column, pier, or pilaster in the form of a draped female figure.

tgm012157.label: Death masks
tgm012157.scope: Search also under the subdivision --DEATH MASK used with names of persons (Appendix B).

tgm012161.label: Microphones
tgm012161.scope: Devices that convert acoustical sound waves into corresponding variations in electrical current that are then amplified, transmitted, or recorded (AAT).

tgm012162.label: Prostitutes
tgm012162.scope: People who sell their services as sexual partners (AAT).

tgm012163.label: Rural areas
tgm012163.scope: Countryside or agricultural areas that are sparsely settled.

tgm012165.label: Holy water stoups
tgm012165.scope: Basins used to contain holy water at the entrance of a church.

tgm012167.label: Rose windows
tgm012167.scope: Circular windows, usually stained glass, containing patterned tracery in the form of a rose or a wheel.

tgm012168.label: Spolia
tgm012168.scope: Reuse of architectural sculpture or fragments, incorporated into a new building or sculpture.

tgm012172.label: Foam
tgm012172.scope: Minute bubbles formed on the surface of liquids.

tgm012221.label: Galleys (Ships)
tgm012221.scope: For large ships with rows of oars on each side, also propelled by sails.

tgm012228.label: Cubicles
tgm012228.scope: Partioned spaces used for work or other functions.

tgm012230.label: Columbaria
tgm012230.scope: Vaults with recessed structures for holding cinerary urns.

tgm012233.label: Widows' walks
tgm012233.scope: A railed rooftop platform, usually found on a coastal home.

tgm012237.label: Boundary walls
tgm012237.scope: Walls which enclose an area or define a border between countries, regions, or properties.

tgm012238.label: Tells
tgm012238.scope: A mound of debris built up from successive layers of human habitation.

tgm012266.label: Spurs
tgm012266.scope: A pointed implement secured to the heel of a rider to urge the horse by its pressure.

tgm012268.label: Fasces
tgm012268.scope: A bundle of rods bound with an axe carried before Roman magistrates symbolizing their power.

tgm012277.label: Powwows
tgm012277.scope: A gathering of Native American people, usually involving dance, music, socializing, and competitions.

tgm012279.label: Orotones
tgm012279.scope: Photographs printed on glass having a rich, warm gold-toned appearance. They are made by exposing a negative to the gelatin emulsion coating on the front of a glass plate on which the back of the plate has been treated with a gold paint or similar substances that possess the qualities of gold-toning.

tgm012280.label: Saddle blankets
tgm012280.scope: A blanket which is placed between the saddle and the back of an animal.

tgm012283.label: Child soldiers
tgm012283.scope: A person under the age of eighteen who is part of a regular or irregular armed force.

tgm012287.label: Zombies
tgm012287.scope: For corpses that have been re-animated by a supernatural power.

tgm012291.label: Writing boards
tgm012291.scope: Boards or tablets upon which one writes or draws.

tgm012292.label: Koranic boards
tgm012292.scope: Writing boards used in Koranic schools upon which pupils write verses from the Koran.

tgm012294.label: Marabouts
tgm012294.scope: Islamic spiritual leaders or teachers in West Africa and the Maghreb.

tgm012296.label: Hose carriages
tgm012296.scope: Firefighting vehicles with large reels for carrying fire hoses, usually horse-drawn.

tgm012309.label: Dog tags
tgm012309.scope: Identification tags, particularly for the identification of pets or members of the military. Military dog tags are typically metal tags worn in pairs by military personnel around their necks, carrying such information as name, rank, serial number, religious affiliation, and blood type, so-called because they broadly resemble the common tags used for pets.

tgm012310.label: Saxhorns
tgm012310.scope: Any of a group of valved brass instruments, ranging from soprano to bass, and characterized by a conical tube, oval shape, and cup-shaped mouthpiece (Websters).

tgm012321.label: Gyalings
tgm012321.scope: A double-reed shawm used in Buddhist rituals in Tibet and Sikkim.

tgm012325.label: Carding
tgm012325.scope: Cleaning, untangling, and gathering fibers together with a hand tool called a card, in order to prepare them for spinning.

tgm012326.label: Prayer flags
tgm012326.scope: Religious banners inscribed with prayers that bless an area when the wind blows over them, used by Buddhists.

tgm012328.label: Catapults (Weapons)
tgm012328.scope: Ancient military devices used to hurl heavy projectiles such as large stones.

tgm012329.label: Yaks
tgm012329.scope: A long-haired bovine animal, found mostly in the Himalayan region.

tgm012337.label: Environmental art
tgm012337.scope: Outdoor contemporary art that surrounds or involves the viewer.

tgm012338.label: Earthworks (Sculpture)
tgm012338.scope: Works that alter the terrain for artistic purposes.

tgm012340.label: Prayer wheels
tgm012340.scope: Cylinder on a spindle used in Buddhist prayer.

tgm012350.label: Diaries
tgm012350.scope: A book of daily entries which chronicles a writer's experiences and observations.

tgm012352.label: Bilderbogen
tgm012352.scope: Broad in scope and purpose, brightly colored, often well executed, though sometimes crude, these illustrations create a visual encyclopedia of social and moral themes intended to appeal to a wide spectrum of society, from sophisticated consumers to rural, less educated groups. Occassionally humorous, more often educational, the picture sheets were a means for disseminating ideas, political agendas, and socially acceptable behavior, as well as providing amusement as pieces to be used as toys.

tgm012354.label: Headscarves
tgm012354.scope: Scarf worn for warmth or for covering the head or face.

tgm012363.label: Garrotes
tgm012363.scope: A device used for execution by strangulation.

tgm012393.label: Whittling
tgm012393.scope: Shaving or paring a piece of wood or bone with a knife.

tgm012394.label: Meteors
tgm012394.scope: Small interplanetary masses that enter the Earth's atmosphere at such high speed that a streak of light or luminous trail appears. If such a mass lands on the ground, it is called a meteorite.

tgm012397.label: Herbalists
tgm012397.scope: For people skilled in the therapeutic use of medicinal plants.

tgm012399.label: Crystoleums
tgm012399.scope: Albumen photographic prints adhered to a concave piece of glass and sanded from the back to remove the paper layer from the emulsion. A layer of oil is applied to render the emulsion translucent. Then, detailed color is applied to the emulsion on the back of the glass and allowed to dry. Next, a second layer of curved glass is placed behind the emulsion and painted with broad fields of color. A layer of white material is then applied behind it and finally the layers are bound together. The process was used from the 1880s through 1910s.

tgm012400.label: Crystalotypes
tgm012400.scope: Salted paper photographic prints from albumen glass negatives. The process was patented by John Whipple in 1850. The albumen glass negatives were sometimes also referred to as Crystalotypes.

tgm012402.label: Crystalographs
tgm012402.scope: Process patented by Henry A. Marchant in 1857 involves an albumen photographic print adhered to a flat piece of glass with a heated mixture of clarified wax, rectified turpentine, and dammar gum. The photograph is then coated with another layer of the mixture, topped with a second piece of glass, and placed in a press until the mixture has solidified, rendering the paper transparent. Pigment is then applied to the back of the glass to color the photograph. The process was not commonly used, possibly because it was so difficult and complicated to produce.

tgm012404.label: Family members
tgm012404.scope: Individuals identified by family relationship. Search also under subdivision --FAMILY used with names of persons (Appendix B).

tgm012405.label: Wings (Anatomy)
tgm012405.scope: Organs of flight of any flying animal such as a bird, bat, or insect.

tgm012407.label: Headphones
tgm012407.scope: Small loudspeakers worn on the head for listening to music or for communications purposes.

tgm012412.label: Sets (Architectural elements)
tgm012412.scope: Scenery, props, and lighting and sound systems created to represent a setting used in a dramatic performance (AAT).

tgm012415.label: Lightning rods
tgm012415.scope: Metal rods or wires placed above the highest point of a roof or chimney of a building for conducting or diverting the electrical charge of lightning away from the building.

tgm012418.label: Jumping jacks (Toys)
tgm012418.scope: Jointed-figure pull-string toys with strings attached at top and bottom that cause the arms and legs to move up and down when the strings are pulled.

tgm012419.label: Ornamental pools
tgm012419.scope: Artificial bodies of water designed to decorate gardens.

tgm012420.label: Flower gardens
tgm012420.scope: Gardens that contain beds or borders of flowers.

tgm012431.label: Buckskins
tgm012431.scope: Clothing, usually jackets and leggings, made of soft leather, and characterized by the presence of fringes or quills along the sleeves and/or legs.

tgm012437.label: Orangeries
tgm012437.scope: A greenhouse, or other sheltered place, that is used for the cultivation of tropical plants, such as orange trees.

tgm012439.label: Lamas
tgm012439.scope: Buddhist priests of Mongolia and the Tibetan territories of southwestern China.

tgm012444.label: Duotone photomechanical prints
tgm012444.scope: Two halftone prints, relief or planographic, from the same monochrome original, given different exposures and printed in different inks.

tgm012445.label: Food fights
tgm012445.scope: For images of people using food as weapons, usually in a humorous situation.

tgm012448.label: Cupcakes
tgm012448.scope: A small cake baked in a cup-shaped foil or paper mold.

tgm012467.label: Grayscale digital images
tgm012467.scope: Digital images of shades of gray only, as revealed in their metadata.

tgm012473.label: Stockades
tgm012473.scope: Defensive enclosures made with posts, stakes, or other timber.

tgm012474.label: Drills (Sports)
tgm012474.scope: Activities that include physical and mental skills to perform systematic sequences of movements.

tgm012480.label: Photograph morgues (Collections)
tgm012480.scope: Collection or archive of photographs taken for and used by news publications.

tgm012487.label: Histograms
tgm012487.scope: Histograms are graphs that display the intensities of tonality for a digital image.

tgm012488.label: Black & white photographs
tgm012488.scope: A general designation that encompasses a variety of photographic processes that produce images in gray, black and white, or sepia tones.

tgm012489.label: Color photographs
tgm012489.scope: A general designation encompassing a variety of photographic processes that produce images across a broad color spectrum.

tgm012490.label: Foreign laborers
tgm012490.scope: For laborers who seek work outside their own country. Search under MIGRANT LABORERS for those who regularly migrate within the same country.

tgm012492.label: Vivandières
tgm012492.scope: Wives and daughters of soldiers attached to military regiments to sell provisions and liquor to troops, especially during the 18th and 19th centuries.

tgm012496.label: Draft (Sports)
tgm012496.scope: Special occassions in sports for the selection or drawing of an individual from a larger group of athletes.

tgm012502.label: Social status
tgm012502.scope: A person's rank within a social hierarchy.

tgm012521.label: Shorthand
tgm012521.scope: A method of writing rapidly using abbreviations and symbols.

tgm012525.label: Camera operators
tgm012525.scope: For people who operate television, video, or motion picture cameras.

tgm012529.label: Chlorophyll prints
tgm012529.scope: Photographs printed using the light-sensitive chlorophyll in leaves.

tgm012549.label: Painted wall signs
tgm012549.scope: An outdoor advertisement painted onto the exterior of a building.

tgm012556.label: Vivat ribbons
tgm012556.scope: Silk ribbons issued to raise money for the Red Cross in World War I, chiefly in Germany and Austria.

tgm012559.label: Ivorytypes
tgm012559.scope: Photographic prints intended to have the appearance of miniature paintings on ivory.

tgm012563.label: Street art
tgm012563.scope: Paintings or drawings on walls, sidewalks, site elements, or streets.

tgm012567.label: Collectibles
tgm012567.scope: Objects of interest to collectors, such as toys, miniatures, spoons, plates, etc.

tgm012571.label: Airlines
tgm012571.scope: Use for companies that provide air-transport services. Includes activities and structures.

tgm012575.label: Global warming
tgm012575.scope: Increase of the average temperature of the earth's lower atmosphere as a result of greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels

tgm012582.label: Muffs
tgm012582.scope: Fur or fabric cylinder with openings at each end, used to keep hands warm.

tgm012583.label: Observation decks
